_note: Run: <torch-venv>/bin/python bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/lejepa-backbone.json --python <torch-venv>/bin/python (an interpreter with torch/timm, so the frozen backbone builds and loads in-process). This is the A3:lejepa wiring (docs/STEP3_PORTING_PLAN.md). Unlike MAE and I-JEPA -- whose hand-written, non-timm encoders each ship their own downstream_backbone.py provider -- LeJEPA trains a standard timm ViT-B/16 whose bare-key encoder.pt loads straight into the shared 'vit' spatial-backbone kind, so a dedicated provider would be an empty duplicate (never implement the same rule twice; a guard with no killed mutant is not a guard). The wiring is therefore a config, methods/37_lejepa/configs/downstream_arssl.json, discovered by structure. These mutations prove the wiring is not vacuous: the config must name the shared vit kind and a real, buildable arch, and the bare-key checkpoint load through that kind must refuse an alien checkpoint rather than half-load it. The alien-key refusal lives in the shared downstream/spatial_backbones.py::_build_vit and was NOT previously mutation-proven (the mae/ijepa specs only touch the dispatch/KINDS/discovery lines); this spec proves it via the LeJEPA path.

targets.label: the wiring config no longer names the shared vit kind (a wrong or unknown kind is accepted)
the config names an arch that is not a real timm model
a checkpoint carrying keys this ViT does not have is half-loaded, not refused

_result.measured_with: an interpreter with torch==2.13.0 + timm (.venvs/05_jigsaw_puzzle), which builds and loads the timm ViT backbone in-process
